identity.title: FAUST. II. Discovery of a Secondary Outflow in IRAS 15398-3359: Variability in Outflow Direction during the Earliest Stage of Star Formation?

paper_type_evidence.quote: We have observed the very low-mass Class 0 protostar IRAS 15398$-$3359 at scales ranging from 50 au to 1800 au, as part of the ALMA Large Program FAUST.

question.value: What are the nature and origin of a newly found arc-like shock structure and linear feature perpendicular to the known outflow of IRAS 15398-3359 (relic secondary outflow, reorientation, binary)?

evidence.quote: The origins of the newly observed arc-like structure and extended linear feature are discussed in relation to turbulent motions within the protostellar core and episodic accretion events during the earliest stage of protostellar evolution.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data set: ADS/JAO.ALMA# 2018.1.01205.L (PI: Satoshi Yamamoto).

findings_qualitative.value: SO, SiO and CH3OH trace an arc-like shocked structure SE of the protostar, blue-shifted from the systemic velocity

evidence.quote: The arc-like structure is blue-shifted with respect to the systemic velocity.

claims.hypothesis: Is the arc-like structure a shocked region from an earlier outflow?
claims.experiment: Moment maps, channel maps, spectra and RADEX abundances of SO, SiO, CH3OH, H2CO vs C18O
claims.result: SO, SiO and CH3OH trace the arc with enhanced abundance ratios comparable to L1157-B1 (lower limits), narrow SiO lines
claims.finding: The arc is a relic shock produced by a previously launched outflow

evidence.quote: SO, SiO, and CH$_3$OH are known to trace shocks, and we interpret the arc-like structure as a relic shock region produced by an outflow previously launched by IRAS 15398$-$3359.

claims.hypothesis: Does the linear feature connect the protostar to the arc kinematically as an outflow?
claims.experiment: PV diagrams of H2CO and C18O along P.A. 140
claims.result: Velocity gradient of 1.2 km/s over 1200 au toward the southeast
claims.finding: The linear structure is a secondary, relic outflow

evidence.quote: The velocity gradient along the linear structure can be explained as relic outflow motion.

claims.hypothesis: Could two outflows from a binary explain the secondary outflow?
claims.experiment: Comparison with earlier ALMA 30 au resolution results and literature on binary outflows
claims.result: Single continuum peak and Keplerian disk at 30 au; no theory for such a close binary with very different rotation axes
claims.finding: Binary hypothesis unlikely, tight binary (<30 au) not excluded

evidence.loc: 5.1 Scenario 1: Two Outflows Driven by a Binary System
evidence.quote: We thus conclude that binary hypothesis for the secondary outflow is unlikely, although we cannot completely rule out the possibility of a tight binary

claims.hypothesis: Can outflow reorientation from episodic accretion with varying angular momentum explain the geometry?
claims.experiment: Dissipation timescale estimate and comparison with models and literature
claims.result: Dissipation timescale ~4000 yr comparable to dynamical timescale ~5000 cot(i) yr
claims.finding: Reorientation of the outflow from a single protostar is proposed as one possible explanation

evidence.quote: We propose the reorientation scenario as one possibility to account for this observation.

referee_caveats_inferred: Gas mass, column densities and timescales rest on assumed H2 densities and temperatures spanning an order of magnitude
Inclination of the secondary outflow is unconstrained, so the timescale is only given as a function of cot(i)
No quantitative fit or uncertainty is given for the velocity gradient
Binary and reorientation scenarios are argued qualitatively without simulations of this system
